Customer: provide sample request/response sizes and 2 weeks of traffic histogram by 2026-05-22
Schedule 48-hour benchmark run the week of 2026-05-25
action_items: Jordan Blake: share Redwood cost model template by 2026-05-21
Priya Nair: propose 3 instance sizing options + quantization recommendation by 2026-05-23

header:
Date: 2026-05-19 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Redwood: Jordan Blake (AE), Priya Nair (SE)
StrataShield: Evan Morales (Platform), Priya Kapoor (Head of AI), Liam O'Connor (CTO)
summary: Kickoff to scope a POC to validate per-token unit economics for an insurance claims triage LLM feature. Main goals: define success criteria (latency/cost/SLA), capture workload size and token distribution, agree on benchmarks and timeline for a 48-hour cost + perf run. Customer emphasized budget ceiling and on-prem constraints for sensitive data.
topics: Success criteria; workload sizing; per-token costing; batching & KV/prefix caching knobs; quantization tradeoffs; bench plan (48h); timelines and next steps
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Blake: yeah hi everyone thanks for joining uh we'll run 45 minutes, kick this off. Can I get quick intros?
00:08 Evan Morales: Evan - platform engineering, I'll own the logs and infra side.
00:12 Priya Kapoor: Priya, head of AI, interested in cost predictability more than anything.
00:16 Liam O'Connor: Liam, CTO, high level oversight.
00:20 Priya Nair: Priya N, SE from Redwood - I'll drive the benchmark and sizing recs.
00:25 Jordan Blake: Cool. Quick agenda: 1) align success criteria 2) workload and token profile 3) bench plan and timing 4) next steps. Sound good?
00:34 Priya Kapoor: Yep, primarily we need to hit a cost target. CFO gave us a ballpark: at scale we need inference cost under $0.003 per API call on average, which maps to unknown per-token thresholds, so we need you to map token econ.
00:47 Jordan Blake: Understood. Can you describe the workload? QPS patterns, typical prompt/response sizes?
00:53 Evan Morales: Sure. It's claims triage - mix of structured form fields + user notes. We expect peak 60 QPS daytime, baseline 8 QPS night, average request is about 250 tokens (prompt+context) and response is 120 tokens. Some longer follow-ups up to 700 tokens.
01:10 Priya Nair: Helpful. We'll convert that to token throughput and give per-token cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated vs private infra. Quick clarification: will PHI be in prompts?
01:20 Priya Kapoor: Minimal PHI. Most PII removed, but full claim text occasionally includes sensitive lines, so we need VPC or private deployment option for the POC — at least private control plane and cloud-hosted inference in a customer VPC.
01:34 Jordan Blake: Noted. Security is doable; we'll include the private deployment pattern in the bench. On the per-token economics, we typically model cost as a function of tokens/sec, batching efficiency, and model family + quantization. For example, on an Llama 2-13B variant quantized to 4-bit, you get X throughput and lower cost vs fp16.
01:55 Liam O'Connor: Can you give a rough per-token estimate now? Even ballpark.
01:59 Priya Nair: Ballpark — for a long-context 13B in our hosted fleet with aggressive batching, you'd see roughly $0.0007 to $0.0015 per 1k tokens depending on latency window and cache hit rate.
02:12 Priya Kapoor: Wait is that per 1k or per token? Sorry.
02:15 Priya Nair: Sorry, per 1k tokens. So per token that's 7e-7 to 1.5e-6. For your 370 token roundtrip average, that'd be around $0.00026 to $0.00056 per call, before any caching or prefix reuse.
02:31 Evan Morales: Hmm CFO wants ~0.003 per call so that seems ok, but that's at hosted, not necessarily private; and we expect regression if we need on-prem.
02:40 Jordan Blake: Right. Private deployments often have higher infra cost — we'll show three scenarios: hosted (best unit econ), dedicated reserved (mid), private customer VPC (higher).
02:49 Priya Kapoor: Another variable is caching: we have a lot of repeated legal boilerplate in prompts. If we can cache prefixes with a high hit rate, that reduces forward compute. Can you model caching impact?
02:58 Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll estimate using two cache hit scenarios: conservative 10% prefix reuse and optimistic 45% reuse. Batching also matters: if you're comfortable with slightly higher p95 latency, we can batch more aggressively and reduce per-token cost.
03:13 Liam O'Connor: What's the latency tradeoff look like numerically? Our SLO is p95 under 400ms for interactive triage UI — can't go above that.
03:23 Priya Nair: For p95<=400ms, batching window needs to be small, so batching efficiency drops, cost goes up. We can provide suggested batch sizes and expected p50/p95 numbers per instance size. In preliminary runs, hitting p95~300ms with 13B quantized gives a certain throughput; we'll include that in the benchmark report.
03:42 Evan Morales: On instrumentation - we can export request timestamps and token counts. We'll also provide sample prompt sets with high-frequency boilerplate to test caching.
03:50 Jordan Blake: Great. Bench plan: Redwood runs a 48-hour benchmark using your traces in our private test VPC simulating your QPS pattern and token sizes. We'll run three model variants (13B q4, 70B q4f16 if you want higher quality, and a smaller 7B) across hosted/dedicated/private configs. We'll measure cost per 1k tokens, latency distribution, cache hit impact, and throughput.
04:15 Priya Kapoor: We definitely want the 13B and 70B comparison; quality is important on edge cases. Also want a human-eval on a subset for regression checks.
04:24 Priya Nair: We'll include a short eval harness with your prompts — 200 adjudicated examples to measure answer quality delta.
04:29 Liam O'Connor: Timeline?
04:31 Jordan Blake: If you can share traces by 2026-05-22 we can schedule the benchmark the week of 2026-05-25 and deliver results within 5 business days after the run.
04:40 Evan Morales: Fine. One more ask: show us a recommended autoscaling/burst policy for Dedicated to keep costs predictable under seasonal spikes.
04:47 Priya Nair: We'll propose autoscale thresholds and a burst capacity plan with cost delta estimates.
04:52 Priya Kapoor: About pricing — do you have a template that maps instance costs, token costs, and amortized infra to per-call? CFO wants a simple per-call spreadsheet.
04:59 Jordan Blake: Yes, that's our cost-model spreadsheet. We'll populate with your trace and show a per-call line item: model compute, GPU amortization, networking, caching savings, and SW overhead.
05:11 Evan Morales: Are there unknowns that will blow up the cost? For example long KV cache misses or hallucinations requiring multiple prompts?
05:18 Priya Nair: Good point. We'll include sensitivity analysis on average tokens per call, cache hit rate, and retrys due to quality. We'll run scenarios to show breakpoints where costs spike.
05:28 Liam O'Connor: Any compliance blockers for the private pattern?
05:31 Jordan Blake: We'll send the security pack: SOC2 artefacts, KMS integration notes, audit logs export. For on-prem we'll note the HSM/KMS guidance.
05:41 Priya Kapoor: Okay let's recap next steps.
05:43 Jordan Blake: Recap: Redwood sends cost model + benchmark plan + security pack by 2026-05-21. StrataShield provides traffic traces, sample prompts, and some eval examples by 2026-05-22. Schedule bench week of 2026-05-25.
05:58 Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Thanks all.
06:02 Jordan Blake: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links.
06:05 [call ends]
